district.name: Tumakuru
district.description: Known as 'Kalpataru Nadu' for its coconut wealth, Tumakuru features Asia's second-largest monolithic Madhugiri Fort, Sri Siddaganga Matha, Devarayanadurga hill temples, and pristine Hoysala temples at Aralaguppe.
district.descriptionKannada: 'ಕಲ್ಪತರು ನಾಡು' ತುಮಕೂರು, ಏಷ್ಯಾದ ಎರಡನೇ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಏಕಶಿಲೆ ಮಧುಗಿರಿ ಕೋಟೆ, ತ್ರಿವಿಧ ದಾಸೋಹಿ ಶ್ರೀ ಸಿದ್ಧಗಂಗಾ ಮಠ, ದೇವರಾಯನದುರ್ಗ ಮತ್ತು ಅರಳಗುಪ್ಪೆ ಹೊಯ್ಸಳ ದೇವಾಲಯಗಳನ್ನು ಒಳಗೊಂಡಿದೆ.

destinations.name: Madhugiri Monolithic Hill Fort
destinations.description: Asia's second-largest monolithic granite hill rising 3,930 feet (1,200m) above sea level, crowned by a formidable multi-tiered medieval fortress with steep gateways (Antaralada Bagilu), grain storehouses, and sheer rock climbs that test human endurance.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Originally built in 1670 CE by Raja Hire Gowda of the Madhugiri Palegars, reinforced by Hyder Ali who added the stone bastions and named it Fatehbagh.
destinations.culturalImportance: A legendary mountain fortress in Karnataka military history, admired for its engineering that merges with bare granite cliff faces.

photos.caption: Madhugiri Monolithic Hill Fort
photos.source: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka Gazetteer

destinations.bestSeason: October to February (Climb early morning; strictly avoid rain)
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: Located at Madhugiri town, 43 km from Tumakuru, 105 km from Bengaluru
destinations.roadAccessibility: Well-paved state highway connecting Tumakuru to Madhugiri
destinations.trekkingDifficulty: Challenging (steep 60-degree granite rock face with rock-cut footholds)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Carry at least 2 liters of water and snacks. Never climb during rain; bare granite becomes slippery. Wear shoes with deep rubber tread.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India; open public entry
destinations.tourismInformationSource: Archaeological Survey of India & Karnataka Gazetteer

destinations.name: Aralaguppe Chennakeshava & Kalleshwara Temples
destinations.description: A quiet village holding two supreme architectural treasures: the 13th-century Hoysala Chennakeshava Temple (1250 CE) featuring a star-shaped stellate plinth with 140 relief panels, and the 9th-century Nolamba Kalleshwara Temple housing an astonishing ceiling sculpture of dancing Nataraja surrounded by Ashta Dikpalakas.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Built by Hoysala master sculptor Honnoja under King Someshwara; Nolamba Kalleshwara ceiling is ranked among India's finest stone reliefs.
destinations.culturalImportance: An untouched heritage oasis free of commercial tourist crowds, preserving pristine 13th-century soapstone artistry.
destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 18 km from Tiptur, 60 km from Tumakuru
destinations.nearestBusStation: Aralaguppe Bus Stop (0.5 km) / Tiptur Bus Stand (18 km)
destinations.nearestRailwayStation: Aralaguppe Railway Station (1 km) on Bengaluru-Hubballi line
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved rural road from Tiptur or Banasandra
destinations.safetyInstructions: Remove footwear before entering temple mandapas. Carry torch to appreciate ceiling carvings.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Protected by Archaeological Survey of India

destinations.name: Sri Siddaganga Matha (Trividha Dasoha Peetha)
destinations.description: A globally revered 600-year-old humanitarian and educational institution established by Sri Gosala Siddeshwara Swamiji in the 15th century. Elevated to global renown by centenarian saint Dr. Sri Sri Shivakumara Swamiji (known as 'Walking God'), who provided free food (Anna Dasoha), shelter (Jnaana Dasoha), and education to over 10,000 underprivileged children daily.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Founded in the 15th century; Dr. Shivakumara Swamiji lived to 111 years and was posthumously awarded the Padma Bhushan for his lifelong service.
destinations.culturalImportance: The living conscience of Karnataka humanitarianism, embodying Basaveshwara's principle of 'Kayaka' (work is worship) and 'Dasoha' (selfless sharing).

photos.caption: Sri Siddaganga Matha (Trividha Dasoha Peetha)
photos.source: Sri Siddaganga Matha Trust & Karnataka Tourism

destinations.trekkingDifficulty: None (easy campus walking; hilltop temple has stairs)
destinations.safetyInstructions: All pilgrims are served free sanctified meals (Dasoha) at the grand community hall. Respect campus cleanliness.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Open to all humanity regardless of caste, creed, or religion

destinations.name: Devarayanadurga Hill Temples & Namada Chilume Spring
destinations.description: A lush 1,200-meter hill station surrounded by reserve forests, housing the 9th-century Bhoga Narasimha Temple at the base and Yoga Narasimha Temple atop the craggy summit. Nearby lies Namada Chilume, a sacred natural spring that sprouted from rock when Lord Rama shot an arrow to apply 'Nama' (tilak) to his forehead.
destinations.historicalSignificance: Renamed Devarayanadurga after Mysore Maharaja Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar captured it in 1696 CE.
destinations.culturalImportance: Sacred hill station rich in medicinal plants, spotted deer, and the annual Car Festival (Jathra) on Chaitra Poornima.

photos.caption: Devarayanadurga Hill Temples & Namada Chilume Spring

destinations.distanceFromNearestTown: 15 km from Tumakuru, 70 km from Bengaluru
destinations.roadAccessibility: Paved ghat road through dense reserve forest
destinations.trekkingDifficulty: Moderate (approx. 200 stone steps to Yoga Narasimha summit)
destinations.safetyInstructions: Monkeys are present; keep food concealed. Deer park adjacent to Namada Chilume has marked viewing areas.
destinations.permissionRequirements: Open access, managed by Endowments & Forest Dept
